thread.title: Google joins Amazon, Apple with major push for operations outside the West Coast

author: Rachel Koning Beals
title: Google joins Amazon, Apple with major push for operations outside the West Coast
text:
Google joins Amazon, Apple with major push for operations outside the West Coast MarketWatch 1 hour ago Rachel Koning Beals © Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Alphabet Inc.’s Google announced a major real-estate expansion in New York City that will make the company one of the city’s largest commercial tenants, and brings a pledge of thousands of new jobs in coming years.
Silicon Valley behemoth Google (GOOGL) said in a blog post it would lease a large office building in Manhattan’s West Village neighborhood and make it the centerpiece of a new 1.7 million-square-foot Hudson Square Campus. Google plans to invest $1 billion in capital improvements to the campus.
The Wall Street Journal reported last month on the company’s New York expansion plans. At that time, Google finance chief Ruth Porat said the internet giant plans to double its New York-based workforce to more than 14,000 employees over the next decade .
© Cookfox Architects A rendering of St.John’s Terminal at 550 Washington St., an office building that Google said Monday it will lease and make the centerpiece of its 1.7 million-square-foot Hudson Square Campus. “When we came to New York City almost two decades ago, it was our first office outside of California. It’s now home to more than 7,000 employees, speaking 50 languages, working on a broad range of teams including Search, Ads, Maps, YouTube, Cloud, Technical Infrastructure, Sales, Partnerships and Research,” Porat said in her Monday blog post.
Google’s ambitions for New York follow those for Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) , which recently selected New York as one of two East Coast locations for major satellite offices expected to employ 25,000 people each by 2028; the other is outside of Washington, D.C. Unlike Amazon, which pitted cities against each other in a contest for favorable tax breaks and other incentives, Google said it hadn’t pursued incentives from New York.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) last week said it plans to invest $1 billion to build a second campus in Austin, Texas, for 5,000 employees .
Google is on track to be among the largest corporate office tenants in Manhattan. Its total footprint in the city is expected to encompass nearly 7 million square feet of owned or leased office space, the Wall Street Journal reports. That’s enough for more than 46,000 total employees, based on the industry standard of 150 square feet per employee and includes buildings where Google still leases space to other tenants as well as plans to expand existing properties. Amazon has announced plans to occupy 4 million to 8 million square feet of office space in the New York City area.
Alphabet’s shares are down 0.4% in the year to date. The S&P 500 (SPX) is down 2.7%.
